nodes.tagline: Physical intelligence for every decision with Geospatial AI.
nodes.description:
Ageospatial helps organizations value the risk on their physical assets (properties, land, infrastructure) remotely using satellite imagery.

97% of commercial properties are never physically inspected because it's too slow and expensive. So insurers price risk based on what the client or broker tells them, and about half the time at least one of those records is wrong. The result is mispricing, fraud, and an estimated $36B in premium leakage every year in the US alone, which gets exposed the moment a disaster hits.

Upload a list of addresses and their GeoAI reads satellite and street-level imagery, maps, real-time data, public records and the insurer's own data to determine what's really there, which natural and human hazards surround it, what changed over time, and which properties are worth inspecting. Each property becomes a living record that underwriting, claims and pricing teams can trace from past to present. Ageospatial deploys inside carriers and MGAs as an AI-native service, so insurers get outcomes delivered.

nodes.tagline: Electrifying North American freight rail with swappable batteries.
nodes.description:
Ailit is building the electric energy system for North American freight rail. Our first product, Superwagon, is a battery wagon designed to power existing diesel-electric locomotives, allowing railroads to electrify the fleets they already own.

Superwagon carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive’s existing electric motors. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones along the route and recharged off-board, providing operators with limitless range.

We deliver energy as a service, owning and operating the batteries and swapping sites. Railroads pay for energy with no upfront equipment purchase, with pricing set at 20% below today’s diesel cost.

Founded in Stockholm by Christian Lind and Emil Tagesson, our team is now based in San Francisco. We’re building our first full-scale prototype, and it’s being prepared to move a locomotive on battery power in the coming days.

nodes.tagline: Stripe for medical billing
nodes.description:
Altair is an AI-native medical billing service for independent practices. We take over a practice's billing end to end and get doctors paid by insurers. AI does the work; our billers handle the exceptions.

That can only work if a practice can trust an agent alone with its revenue. So we formalized insurers' billing policies and put a theorem prover under the agent. Before the agent acts on a claim, the prover checks the action against that insurer's policies, and anything that fails goes to one of our billers. 

Every claim teaches Altair how each insurer behaves, so the longer we run a practice's billing, the better we predict what its insurers will pay, deny or delay.

We're building the default way a new practice gets paid: a doctor connects their EHR and bills clean, completely self-serve and on auto-pilot.

Altair will be the financial platform every independent practice in America starts on and stays on. And to the Health Insurers' "Delay, Deny, Defend", we say "Predict, Prevent, Prevail".

nodes.tagline: Continuous security verification for AI in regulated industries
nodes.description:
Armorer helps companies in regulated industries ship their own AI systems faster and keep them secure in production.

Most security tools flag an issue and file a ticket. Armorer assesses your agent and simulates attacks to find the real issues. Then it creates a verified fix that stops the attack without breaking the business, ready for your approval in about 4 hours.

In production, Armorer checks every agent action in milliseconds, with no GPU needed. It detects malicious behavior such as prompt injection, goal hijacking and data leaks, then allows, holds or denies the action.

Armorer's detection models beat every other detector we tested on six public benchmarks. Armorer is 22% more accurate than JEV while being 88x faster, so users won't feel the delay.

We spent years building and evaluating AI security systems together at AWS, including its first customer-facing AI security agent, which scaled to 100k+ customers. Armorer is backed by Paul Vixie, an internet pioneer inducted into the Internet Hall of Fame in 2014.

nodes.tagline: Custom software for senior care facilities.
nodes.description:
Ascenix is building one custom interface for running senior homes. We combine reusable building blocks into workflows tailored to each home's existing processes, from incident reporting to reimbursement. Homes get custom software without hiring an engineering team.

Living in a retirement home convinced us that the best way to improve residents' lives is to improve the systems staff rely on. As the older population grows, care teams need more time and resources. Repetitive reporting, missed reimbursement, and compliance problems take those away. Disconnected products that solve each of these individually add costs and leave staff moving information between systems.

Our building blocks gather information from EHRs like PointClickCare and other sources, process it, apply rules, and produce reports, tasks, or emails. Incident reporting and reimbursement reviews usually come from two separate vendors. Ascenix builds both from the same blocks, in one interface, so data isn't stuck in silos. Homes start with their biggest bottleneck and add workflows as priorities change.

nodes.tagline: The best cloud VMs for billions of agents
nodes.description:
**Problem**

Humans used to need laptops to do their work. Now they prompt agents instead, and those agents need computers too: always-on, in large quantities, and with unlimited capabilities. 

Building and maintaining that yourself is far from trivial.

**Solution**

Boat provides powerful, simple, permissive Ubuntu VMs in the cloud. In a sandbox, an agent can work for long periods on code or on knowledge work like legal, research, reporting, and auditing.

**Why Boat and not any other cloud VM?**

1. It is ready out of the box: every sandbox ships with a desktop, chrome, languages, docker, snapshots, and templates, plus a CLI, SDK, API, and control pane for your fleet.
2. It is permissive and paradigm agnostic: any number of agents can use any number of sandboxes. Agents can run inside or use sandboxes as an external tool.
3. It is expertly crafted: we manage everything from the individual CPU to the orchestration software, which makes sandboxes stable, persistent, scalable, and secure.
4. It is the best performance and price in town: our CPUs rank first on HPC benchmarks, and sandboxes are typically 9x to 18x cheaper than other leading sandboxes.

**Further notes**

Sandboxes are hosted in Europe, which keeps prices low, and more regions are coming. Unless compliance requires it, agents don't notice the region they run in.

nodes.tagline: Connect operational data with finance to see what drives the numbers.
nodes.description:
Definite connects operational data with finance so businesses that make, move, build or operate things can see what each production run, load and job actually cost.

These businesses already record a lot: production runs, shipments, job sites, equipment hours, work orders. Finance records the same business in a different shape. Operating systems track activity by site, line, or day. The ledger tracks it by entity, account, and month. Both sets of records exist, but the link between an operating decision and its financial effect usually lives in spreadsheets and in a few people's heads.

So questions that should be routine take days. What happens to cash if one plant adds a shift? How does a change in throughput or staffing flow into the forecast? Which operating changes actually moved the numbers last quarter?

Definite connects to existing operational and financial systems read-only. Models propose how operational records map to financial ones and explain what they find. Deterministic rules perform the calculations and checks, so results trace back to the source records they came from. 

Definite started in a plant office an hour from campus, watching a controller rebuild the same spreadsheet she rebuilds every month to tie her production system to her ledger. The three of us met at the University of Waterloo and had each spent our careers on a version of that join. Gurshabd built wallet policy and approval controls at BitGo, where proving customer assets matched the ledger was still done by hand. Farhan built recommendation systems for Instagram Reels at Meta, joining billions of raw events to the numbers the business reported. Mazin built trading systems at Optiver, then agents for financial analysts at Boosted.ai, where analysts would not act on a number they could not trace. In finance that work is at least funded. In companies that make and move things, nobody had built it at all.

🔥FIRE WALLET 🔥

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JeXDDegwhgA

TL;DR: Fire Wallet is a fast, end-to-end encrypted, non-custodial stablecoin wallet with built-in payment processing and fiat on/off ramps, built by the team that created MobileCoin, the cryptocurrency inside Signal.

Hey Bookface! We're Josh, Michael, and Manny and we're building Fire Wallet!

Most wallets and payment processors don’t work FOR you. They're slow, route your payments in the way that earns them the most, and they leak your financial life to anyone asking. Worse: every single one hold the keys to your money.

nodes.tagline: building the open agent runtime
nodes.description:
Developers don't run one coding agent anymore. They run fleets of them — for hours, sometimes days — across laptops, servers, and sandboxes. Keeping track of that work is the new bottleneck: which agent is blocked, which one finished, which terminal is it in, and why did everything die when the laptop closed.

Herdr is the open-source home for that work. A background server owns the agents' terminal sessions on each machine, so the work survives disconnects, closed lids, and dropped SSH. Herdr detects each agent and turns the chaos into an attention queue — working, blocked, done, across every project — so you look only when an agent needs you. Every client is just a view: the bundled terminal UI, SSH from another machine, your phone. Close one, open another; the work never stops.

Software can drive it too: a CLI, a socket API, and a plugin marketplace that passed 500 community plugins in its first month. The runtime is Apache-2.0 and stays open. Four months after launch: 25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads.

nodes.tagline: 100% automated inspection for precision hardware parts
nodes.description:
Hundred is an automated inspection system for the components that make up devices like phones, smartwatches, and laptops. Hundred helps factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-100µm visual defects before parts reach the assembly line. 

Designs change so fast that traditional machine vision can't keep up, forcing factories to rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss roughly 15% of defects, and a single bad part can turn a finished device into scrap. Hundred is replacing manual inspection with an imaging rig that scans an entire shipping tray of parts at once. 

The Hundred rig blocks ambient light and uses varied controlled lighting configurations to detect defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials. The controlled environment means Hundred only needs to scan a single good part before it can find defects, categorize them, and assess their severity accurately.

Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, a problem Hundred's CEO, Erica, saw firsthand as a mechanical engineer designing devices at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani, Hundred's CPO, at Columbia University's admitted-students day in 2017 and Imani went on to spend five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day. Erica later met Iris, Hundred's CTO, in the Bay Area. Iris worked as a quant at Citadel before pivoting to study at Imperial College London where she researched machine learning on 3D meshes and other structured data. Together, they're building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't still exist in 2026.

nodes.tagline: Stop AI agent mistakes by reading the model’s mind
nodes.description:
Latent is a control layer for AI, built on interpretability. It reads signals inside a model as it works and checks every answer and agent action in milliseconds. Then it lets the output through, holds it, re-asks a stronger model, or sends it to review with the reason attached.

Reading the model is far cheaper than running a second LLM, so it can check every step. Latent stops 99% of rule-breaking agents before they act, against 69% for a frontier LLM judge.

It works with self-hosted and API models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini, runs hosted or in your own cloud, and calibrates to your traffic with every review.

nodes.tagline: Engineering the future of Cancer Drug Discovery
nodes.description:
NxtCure Labs is an AI-native, full-stack CRO built to take therapeutics from discovery to market faster. We are reinventing medicine from lab to drug discovery.

About 2 million Americans are diagnosed with cancer every year. Science has never moved faster, new immunotherapies, targeted drugs and cancer vaccines arrive every year. But roughly 90% of cancer drugs fail in clinical trials, and about 80% of trials run late. The breakthroughs exist. The way we test them is stuck in the last century.

NxtCure is building autonomous clinical trials. Before a single patient enrolls, we run the trial thousands of times on digital twins. Each virtual patient is a system of coupled differential equations that track how a drug moves through plasma, tumor and heart, and how the tumor grows, shrinks or fights back. The parameters are fit to real trial data, so every twin behaves like real biology. Across thousands of simulations we can calculate the odds that a dose will hit its endpoints, and fix the protocol before it costs anyone time, money or hope.

Then 13 AI agents run the trial. Each one owns a stage: drafting the protocol, ranking sites, pre-screening patients, forecasting drug supply, watching for adverse events, predicting dropout, cleaning data and writing the final report. As real data comes in, the twins update and flag problems weeks before a human would see them.

In 2025, the FDA laid out how computer simulation can take its place. Soon a cancer drug will run through thousands of simulated trials before it ever touches a lab, and reach patients years faster. We’re building that future.

nodes.tagline: Enable enterprises to ship agent code without human review

Plover Labs is building toward a future where AI agents write, ship, and maintain most of a company's software. We make it possible for agents to own real engineering roles, not just suggest code for someone else to approve.

Coding models keep getting more capable, but enterprise adoption lags behind AI-native startups because enterprises don't yet trust agent output. As the gates build up, agents can be trusted with more of the work.

We have five-figure monthly contracts with Series C companies Envoy and Fieldguide. At Fieldguide, we tripled PRs per engineer in one quarter, with the same headcount and PR size.

nodes.tagline: RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time
nodes.description:
Reific builds RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time, for the frontier labs that train agents. AI has learned to reason over text and code. But most of what matters in the real world shows up as numbers that change every second: a heartbeat, a gearbox, a GPU cluster. No human can track thousands of signals at once, but AI should be able to.

In our environments, data streams in on a clock while the agent works, and every action is graded by what actually happened. Most AI training today teaches models to match human experts. We treat human performance as the floor. Each environment comes from real, de-identified records, in three task families: personal agents, industry, and science & compute.

Today, even the best frontier model averages under 50% on each family. Training an open model on our environments raised its full-solve rate on unseen tasks by 54% (from 25.6% to 39.5%), with no loss on general benchmarks. Our mission is to build the infrastructure that keeps AI climbing the frontier, long past human level in the real world.

nodes.tagline: World's Earliest Test for Alzheimer's Biomarkers
nodes.description:
Alzheimer's testing today is bottlenecked around the onset of symptoms, when the damage is already done. Current treatments, including the FDA-approved drugs released in 2024, don't reverse the disease; they only slow it down. Earlier detection means earlier intervention.

Eye movement changes linked to Alzheimer's surface sooner than any other biomarker, up to 15 years before symptoms appear.

We deliver a 15-minute VR assessment delivered to patients in longevity clinics:
• Tasks: patients perform visual tasks designed by neurologists to trigger a distinct oculomotor response in people with Alzheimer's or on its path
• Hardware: our patent-pending attachment connects to any VR headset on the market and captures these eye movement patterns.
• Analysis: the patterns are compared against our ML model to produce a risk analysis.

Once classified, patients can access new interventions, such as the FDA-approved drugs. They're also referred to longevity practices, neurology practices or both, depending on their stage of decline.

Testing for the earliest biomarkers allows the earliest possible intervention. In some cases, that slows the disease enough that patients outlive the onset of symptoms and never face memory loss in their lifetime.

nodes.tagline: On-device AI that knows your entire life and does your work overnight.
nodes.description:
Truly personal AI requires running inference on your life, every day. In the cloud, that’s expensive and a privacy nightmare. On your own chip, it’s free and private.

Our custom inference stack, built on a LiteRT-LM fork, runs on Macs with just 8 GB of RAM. Every night, Sentient’s on-device models process your emails, messages, Granola transcripts, files, and more, building a rich personal knowledge base on your Mac.

Your projects, conversations, commitments, and preferences. Context you’d never have the time to type into a chatbot.

That understanding powers three ways to get work done:

Sidekick: click your Mac’s notch and say “finish this for me.” It already has your context and gets to work across your apps and browser with its own cursor, while you keep working.

Proactive intelligence: wake up to work already prepared. The reply you forgot, drafted. The subscription renewing tomorrow, caught. The report you promised, ready for review. Sentient waits for your approval before acting.

Double Tap: two taps, two seconds, and the reply you would have written appears, drafted from your personal context and writing style. Just review and send.

Open source and built with privacy at its core. Over 30 enterprises use Sentient already.

Our alpha reached 4,000+ users in its first week with $0 marketing. Our launch was the top post of the month on r/macapps.

We’ve raised over $1 million with participation from Y Combinator (F26), Afore, Pioneer Fund, and a16z speedrun’s scout fund.

nodes.tagline: Virtual machines for long-running agents
nodes.description:
Superserve gives every AI agent its own computer in the cloud. Each one is an isolated VM that starts in under 50ms, sleeps between turns, and picks up exactly where it left off, for hours, weeks or indefinitely.

Traditional cloud infrastructure was built to run one app for many users. Agents flip that. Each agent needs its own isolated machine where it can write and run code, use tools and work on its own for long stretches. Everything it produces has to persist the whole time, the way your laptop keeps your work.

That means agent computers have to be stateful, secure and cheap to run. For agents that talk to customers, they also have to start, sleep and wake almost instantly.

Fast - Machines start in under 50ms, either cold or from a template with your repo and dependencies already loaded. You don't need to keep a pool of servers running and waiting.

Persistent - Paused machines keep their full memory and disk state at zero compute cost. They can resume or fork from that exact state. Pausing and resuming is fast enough that a machine can sleep between inference calls and wake on the next turn. Agents can run Docker, databases, browsers or any other service inside.

Secure - Every machine is a microVM with its own kernel. You can program the rules for what traffic can come in and go out, and they're enforced at the network boundary where the agent can't reach them. API secrets are handled at the network layer too, so they never enter the machine. Every action is logged for audits.

Teams building coding agents, autonomous workers, and eval or RL training environments use Superserve to give every agent session or rollout its own machine, with no infrastructure to manage.

We run 100K+ machines every week for teams including Lindy and Y Combinator.

nodes.tagline: The Microsoft of the AI era: the operating system for AI agents.
nodes.description:
Tilo gives AI agents one shared computer. Today every agent gets its own virtual machine and works by screenshots and clicks, which is slow, expensive and brittle. Agents that work together have to describe what they did to each other in messages.

Tilo is a Linux-based operating system built for agents as users. Every app exports typed actions that agents call over MCP while people use the same actions as buttons, on the same live state. Many agents work in one workspace at once and read each other's work instead of messaging about it. Every change is attributed and can be undone, and irreversible actions need permission. Because state and interface are separate, agents can generate an app's entire UI on demand.

On the same multi-app task with the same model, agents on Tilo were about 29× cheaper and 90× faster than computer use, which failed. A small model on Tilo did it for about 1/10,000 of the frontier model's cost. In our scale test, 50 agents worked in one shared workspace on a single laptop, at about 60 MB of memory per agent. Tilo runs headless, in our cloud, or as a desktop, and you can open any workspace from the browser.

nodes.tagline: Next generation gas turbines for data centers & aviation
nodes.description:
Viraj Aero builds gas turbines that deliver both power and cooling water for data centers. It needs no grid connection and no water pipeline.

Burning natural gas already produces water. Our patented system captures that water from the exhaust. Part of it cools the data center. The rest is turned into steam and injected back into the turbine. That gives up to 40% more power from the same fuel (cheaper compute) and cuts NOx emissions by up to 99%, which cuts permit approvals from years to weeks.

We're building a genset around our first-of-its-kind gas turbine. It fits in a 10-foot container and runs anywhere, even in the desert. That matters because two-thirds of new data centers are being built in water-stressed regions.

We first built this steam-injected turbine for aircraft, where carrying water tanks isn't an option and efficiency is critical. We're currently integrating our full-scale prototype into an aircraft. The team comes from GE, Rolls-Royce and Formula 1, and we're already working with Safran, one of the world's largest aircraft engine manufacturers.

Feels pretty surreal to be writing this, after building, shipping, selling and figuring things out the hard way.

biggestContribution.text:
Introducing Summer Engine (YC F26). Summer makes it easy for everyone to make and play games together!

You ask for the game you want. Summer builds it, and you play it with your friends.

Last Christmas I tried to make a game with AI. The game looked great. But, then I wanted real multiplayer, analytics and monetization, and it became a huge pain! And don't get me started on publishing.

A year later it is still the same for most people. The games look much better, but you still get stuck with a prototype.

So we fixed it.

Today, tens of thousands of creators from all over the world have built games on Summer. The community has made more than 240,000 assets that every user can build with, making it one of the biggest free asset libraries in the world.

You own the game you make on Summer. You can sell it and publish it on Steam, Web, iOS, Android, and on Summer Games.

Making games should be as fun as playing them.

Try it at 
http://
summerengine.com

PS. 
@garrytan
 made a game in a weekend about being a founder in the YC batch. You can try "FounderStar" on the link above.

biggestContribution.text:
We got into 
@ycombinator
 to fix how AI makes music.
 
Today we're launching Taan v1-preview, the most controllable foundation music model.

Music models today make catchy tracks, but you can't steer them. Ask for "violin at exactly the 11th second" and they usually skip it. So you regenerate over and over and hope one take fits. 

Taan is trained to fix this.
 
Hum a melody, name exact notes, or hand it an image, a MIDI file, a video or a script. Taan composes music that fits your context and follows your instructions.
 
v1-preview has genre support limited to orchestral and cinematic music, with more genres on the way.

live today 👇

There’s only 1 industrial robot for every 66 manufacturing workers worldwide.

Manufacturers want to automate. But getting robots onto factory floors is only half the battle.

Production changes. Parts change. Yet teaching a robot something new can still mean calling in a robotics engineer to reprogram it on an old ahh teach pendant.

In robotics, deployment is the moat.

That’s why we started Odin Robotics (YC F26).

We deploy robotic systems, integrate them into existing production lines, and make them easy for factory teams to control and adapt as production changes.

LFG!! 🦾

1- me battling to finish a PR before the factory closes at 2am (before the 5am shift)
2- us posing in the middle of nowhere in Illinois with a gigantic American flag, no sleep
3- even the moustache needs covering before you enter the factory

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but it still takes significant engine
biggestContribution.text:
Today I'm announcing Workers IO to solve the slowest part of engineering, verification!

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but it still takes significant engineering effort to verify what’s being built.

It’s impossible to predict all scenarios that could lead to a failure and that’s why most expensive failures are found in production.

Workers IO runs millions of simulated production scenarios on your entire system, including dependencies. These simulations run inside a deterministic hypervisor which injects faults like network delays, disk errors, clock skew, and process failures to verify how your system handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows us to systematically explore the state space of the system and perfectly reproduce failures.

We are already helping customers do years worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

If you are working on systems that you can never afford to break, DM me and we can help you battle test them!

We’re gearing up to finish F26 strong before Demo Day soon.

To the moon 🚀

biggestContribution.text:
I'm running an AI cloud company alone, shipping about 80 commits per day and spending $1k+ on tokens. It's fair to call "Human in the loop".

Recently I saw a lot of posts about AI-pilled companies out there and I thought that 
@munitoai
 probably deserves a post of its own.

I'm definitely not claiming that it's the most productive setup ever, but very few people I know personally (most of them at 
@ycombinator
 or 
@MistralAI
) or on X are able to ship at the same speed, even now.

Working on a company alone means that you have to wear multiple hats:

- engineer - the obvious one and the one closest to my heart
- GTM - the person that does your sales is also you
- partnership management - we work with a lot of cloud providers and it's a lot of negotiation
- business development - what are we going to ship next?
- tech support - when you serve real customers you have real problems
- marketing - oh, someone has to make cool launch videos or some shit posts (like this one)

All of that for 1 person wasn't possible 2 years ago, but now with all the agents and AI anyone who concentrates on a mission can get it done. Not everything comes out perfectly: software has bugs, videos are sometimes sloppy, partners could be unhappy with you. But it's still possible and this is what is amazing nowadays.

Sam Altman famously said that we will see 10-person billion-dollar companies and I truly believe that we're already there.

So here's my setup that I hope might be useful for someone else.

1. Company brain.
First and foremost, you have to get all your company information in 1 place. Good candidates are 
@NotionHQ
, 
@obsdmd
 or just a git repo. There's a lot of startups and software that try to disrupt the space:

- 
https://
thecompany.company by 
@thecompanyai
 (YC F26)
- 
https://
github.com/yc-software/qm (YC software too)
- 
https://
gbrain.io by 
@gbrainio
, Garry Tan's version of QM :)

However, as I write a lot of code I never managed to truly onboard myself to one of those tools and just went with a git repo. Actually, I got a lot of inspiration from my time at 
@Airbnb
 where we had this repo and a tool called airlab. It was the first thing that you needed to install on your laptop, and then this airlab tool would clone all other company repos in the right directories and all tools would work nicely together. So I went for a similar approach:

- I have a repo called hq and this repo hosts a meta agents.md with company-wide instructions about how agents should work in the repo
- hq/repos is the place where code repositories are actually cloned. I only have 2: monorepo (very originally named) and infra (another original name)
- hq/wiki hosts general information about the company and what is going on in general
- hq/skills - company-wide skills
- hq/automations - some scheduled jobs in a common format that works for Codex and Claude Code
- hq/tools - general tooling to tie it all together

This gives me a nice monorepo feeling without actually being a monorepo. Why it's important will actually be clear from the next point.

2. Agents that understand the whole picture.
When I'm not supporting open models (Hermes from 
@NousResearch
 is one love) I'm a low-key 
@AnthropicAI
 fan. However, at YC we've got "unlimited" credits for 
@OpenAI
 and 
@grok
 too, so all my setup is agent-agnostic and works well no matter what agent I pick.

So I just launch all my agents at the root of hq and with the right instructions they have access to the company data and to all the infra and coding setup.

One of the downsides of that, and why Anthropic plays better than OpenAI there, is that I have a lot of things in the context directly (all the skills, MCPs, etc.) and OpenAI's context of 256k gets overloaded quite quickly. This is why I mostly use Anthropic or Munito's 
@deepseek_ai
 for long-running complex tasks.

3. Schedules and hooks.
All desktop agents support schedules in one form or another and I use all of them.

- OpenAI for quick checks on the infra health, running some light smoke tests.
- Claude Code is my SRE on-call. Whenever something breaks it receives a call from our monitoring stack, investigates and fixes it.
- Hermes on Munito is shipping daily fixes / features from our long-running todo list.
- Grok bot, while not that useful for coding tasks, is a surprisingly good personal assistant and organizer. I use it to review my meeting notes, update client and investor CRMs, as well as scout socials and suggest content ideas.

4. Using agents for everything.
The first thing I look at while trying to pick software (like a CRM for example) is MCP / CLI support. Agents become my interface to the world and I'm looking for tools that are made for agents. Now, I totally see what people are talking about when they say we will just be using an agent as an operating system at some point.

5. A lot of guardrails and testing.
The full testing suite was one of the first things I implemented. Pre-commit checks, unit tests, integration tests, CI, smoke tests, quality control, vulnerability scans. All of this is automated and runs on every change shipped. Only this gives me confidence that things work as intended. However, an interesting observation from my YC group is that nobody reads or reviews code anymore, it's easier to ship a change behind a feature flag, test it and validate that it works than reviewing code written by agents.

A few stats as a conclusion, over 60 days:

- I (we?) produced 2.5M lines of code
- averaged 80 commits a day
- $48k Anthropic credits, $16k of OpenAI credits, $500 (yes open-models are that cheap) of Munito credits.

This sounds like a lot but is it really? I know for sure that there are people in my YC batch that are maxing out their OpenAI allowances of ~500k in 3 months. I cannot imagine what they're building with that!

As a bonus there's a picture of my real working setup now (a lot of people were worried about my health after my previous post)!

A few stats as a conclusion, over 60 days:

- I (we?) produced 2.5M lines of code
- averaged 80 commits a day
- $48k Anthropic credits, $16k of OpenAI credits, $500 (yes open-models are that cheap) of Munito credits.

This sounds like a lot but is it really? I know for sure that there are people in my YC batch that are maxing out their OpenAI allowances of ~500k in 3 months. I cannot imagine what they're building with that!

As a bonus there's a picture of my real working setup now (a lot of people were worried about my health after my previous post)!

biggestContribution.title: San Francisco’daki arkadaşlarım için gelistirdigim bu yöntem sayesinde arkadaşlarım 20 iş başvurusundan 10 dönüş aldılar.
biggestContribution.text:
San Francisco’daki arkadaşlarım için gelistirdigim bu yöntem sayesinde arkadaşlarım 20 iş başvurusundan 10 dönüş aldılar.
Normalde bu oran 20’de 1’di.

Peki nedir bu yöntem?
1. Çalışma izniniz olduğu veya çalışma izni çıkarılması zor olmayan bir ülkede, iş gerekliliklerinin en azından %50’sini karşıladığınız iş fırsatları bulun.
2. CEO'nun röportajlarını, şirket hakkında çıkan haberleri okuyun. Bu soruları cevaplayın:
Şirketin kısa/ uzun vade hedefleri nelerdir?
Bu hedefler doğrultusunda başvurduğunuz ekip şu an hangi sorunu çözmeye çalışıyordur?
3. Ekibin bu sorunu çözmesine nasıl bir katkınız olacağını, ilk 3 ay içinde neler yapabileceğinizi düşünün.
4. Bir ön yazı hazırlayın:
Ön yazıda neler olmalı?
-- Ekibin hangi sorun üzerine çalıştığını tahmin ettiğinizi söyleyin.
-- İşe başladığınızın ilk üç ayınızda bu sorunu çözmek için neleri yapacağınızı anlatın
-- En sonunda İKİ cümleyle kendinizi tanıtın.
Ön yazıda neler olmamalı?
-- Kendinizi ‘çalışkan’, ‘yenilikçi’ gibi güzel sıfatlarla tanımlamayın.
-- ‘Bu alanda kendimi geliştirmek istiyorum’ gibi söylemlerden kaçının.

Unutmayın… Herkes kendine güzel sıfatlar yakıştırabilir. Ve bu aşamada önemli olan, senin kariyerin için ne istediğin değil, onlara ne sunabileceğin.

5. Bu ön yazıyı ekleyip iş başvurusunu yapın.
6. LinkedIn’den, o ekibin ve ilişkili IK’nın yöneticilerinin isimlerini bulun. Ardından VoilaNorbert gibi sitelerden onların emaillerini bulun. Ön yazınızın mail halini onlara yollayın. (Maile ekleme olarak değil, direk kopyala yapıştır yapın.) (2 kişiye) CV’nizi ise direk maile ekleyin.
7. Hubspot’un email izleme aracını bilgisayarınıza yükleyin. Emailinizin açılıp açılmadığını takip edin. Eğer emailiniz açılmıyorsa o ekipten başka birine veya başka bir IK yöneticisine mailinizi yönlendirin.
8. Eğer mailiniz açılıyorsa ama cevap almıyorsanız, hatırlatma mailleri yollayın. Satışta ‘büyülü’ rakam 5’tir. Evet, utanmaca yok, tatlı hatırlatmalara devam edin. Amacımız bir cevap almak. Ya ‘Hayır’ ya ‘Evet.’

İlginizin ve emeğinizin karşılıksız kalmayacağını, geri dönüşlerinizin arttığını göreceksiniz.

Herkese iyi haftalar diliyorum!

-
'Hayalindeki O İş' adlı 8 sayfalık, ücretsiz e-rehberime ulaşmak isterseniz yorumlardaki linke tıklayabilirsiniz. Kendi işe alım ve iş başvurusu tecrübelerimden ve profesyonel kontaklarımın tecrübelerinden yararlanıp sizler için hazırladım. 👇🏻

RATLOG is backed by Y Combinator 🚀

We're building reusable heavy-lift rockets, and we're moving fast. 🚀

Launch prices are rising again, up to $15,000 per kg, and satellite companies wait 3–4 years for a launch slot. That kills most space businesses before they ever fly.

So we designed a new rocket engine from scratch with 90% less complexity, so we can move faster than anyone else in building and launching our rocket.

It took us 4 months from the first part to a finished engine and test stand, built in an 8 m² basement at the YETI Fellowship HQ, to actually hot-fire it.

Now we're in San Francisco for the Fall 2026 batch.

Thank you to the YETI Fellowship, Thomas Kirchner, Sebastian Schuon and Schub for backing us very early and helping us all the way. And to Kulveer Taggar and Y Combinator for betting on the team that did its YC interview partially out of a dark barn on our test site.

Building satellites and need a ride to orbit? DM me. 🛰️

We're proud to announce the close of our $1.3M Pre-seed round to accelerate commercialization of our dual-use electric off-road powertrain technologies. 

To our early believers - thank you for your continued support. 

And to those learning about us now - we're excited to have you along for the ride. 

We'd like to extend a huge thank you to our visionary round lead Boost VC, who saw the potential of what we're building in 2 short conversations. 

We're also extremely excited to welcome on board the perfect early-stage defense investor Harpoon, who are experts with nondilutive funding, military use cases and government go-to-market strategy. 

Another notable strategic investor in our round is the resourceful and rapidly expanding Quorum Capital Partners, who continuously introduce us to subject matter experts in our space. 

Our earliest strategic investor - Goken America - brings over 20 years of automotive design experience, and will be an extremely valuable engineering resourcing partner as our list or projects grow.

Innovation Works invested as part of the AlphaLab Gear hardware accelerator, enabling us to develop and build our proof-of-concept vehicle, and continues to serve as a rapid prototyping resource. 

To the 9 angel investors and multiple advisors who believed in us enough to give us your time and trust us to multiply your capital - thank you. 

Last but certainly not least, the largest thank you goes to our dedicated team members who enabled this fundraise to happen, and who are building the future of the off-road industry every day.

#electricoffroad #EVUTV #SuperPowersMobility #SPM

biggestContribution.text:
I’m excited to announce that, in less than a year, RetireHub has gone from 0 to over 300,000 members. 

The problem we set out to solve was simple: planning for retirement is extremely complex. 

From figuring out personal finances, to navigating the healthcare system, to trying to maximize travel and experiences with loved ones (you know, what retirement is supposed to be about) — there wasn’t one central, trustworthy place that you could go to get all the resources you need. 

Until RetireHub.

We have a long way to go to get all the resources 50+ year olds need, but it’s nice to see our early offerings and content resonate with so many Americans so quickly.

biggestContribution.title:
Last week was a big milestone for the Aikido team as we officially kicked off A1DC — what we believe will be the world's first floating wind-powered datacenter.

This project will take us from the swampy, humid bayou of Louisiana to the frigid fjords of Norway. And last week our team members were in both locations. 

In Louisiana, retrofit activities began on the A1 platform with our fabrication partner MORRISON Energy. Our fearless CEO Sam Kanner, who may get a bit too involved, and our tireless Lead Engineer Jonathan Nash were on site assisting. One lesson learned already: designing for rapid assembly also makes for impressively fast disassembly.

Meanwhile our Norwegian team members were in Haugesund, Norway sharing the details of our project at Floating Wind Days, with our local partners Norwegian Offshore Wind.  

A1DC is an important step toward demonstrating how offshore wind and AI infrastructure can be deployed together in a new way.
We'll be sharing more details on the project soon. Stay tuned.

Introducing Dualizer (YC F26)!

We’re building a physics-grounded AI platform for chemical and industrial process simulation and optimization.

Today, understanding and improving complex industrial processes still requires engineers to manually piece together process diagrams, equipment information, operating data, and specialized simulation tools. Turning that information into rigorous models—and then using those models for design, scale-up, and optimization—is slow and fragmented.

Dualizer combines first-principles engineering with AI and machine learning to help engineers understand complex process systems, build and modify rigorous models, and identify better design and operating strategies faster.

Our goal is to make the physical world easier to understand, design, and optimize.

We’re excited to be part of Y Combinator’s F26 batch in Christopher Golda’s group, and recently won the $100,000 grand prize at Texas A&M’s AI Venture Velocity Challenge, placing 1st out of 531 teams nationwide.

If you’re working on a difficult process problem in chemicals, materials, energy, or other process industries, we’d love to talk.

More to come from Dualizer.

biggestContribution.title:
An AI agent did everything right and still let a customer down.

A retired teacher needed to pay his granddaughter’s college fee, so he asked his bank’s AI assistant to break a sav
biggestContribution.text:
An AI agent did everything right and still let a customer down.

A retired teacher needed to pay his granddaughter’s college fee, so he asked his bank’s AI assistant to break a savings deposit early and move the money to his account.

The AI found the right deposit, closed it, moved the exact amount and told him it was done.

But it never mentioned the penalty for closing early, and it never asked if he still wanted to go ahead, even though a short overdraft could have covered the fee for much less.

And the tests companies run before putting agents in front of customers would still mark this as a pass, because most of them only check the final records.

A database remembers what an agent changed, but it has no trace of the warning it never gave or the question it never asked.

On a banking test with 1,000 tasks, checking only the final records made every model look 6.5 to 12 points better than it really was.

And that’s a big blind spot, because an agent can get every record right and still fail the person it’s working for.

So when you test an agent, check what it should have said and asked along the way, as well as what it changed at the end.

Full breakdown here

An AI agent did everything right and still let a customer down.

A retired teacher needed to pay his granddaughter’s college fee, so he asked his bank’s AI assistant to break a savings deposit early and move the money to his account.

The AI found the right deposit, closed it, moved the exact amount and told him it was done.

But it never mentioned the penalty for closing early, and it never asked if he still wanted to go ahead, even though a short overdraft could have covered the fee for much less.

And the tests companies run before putting agents in front of customers would still mark this as a pass, because most of them only check the final records.

A database remembers what an agent changed, but it has no trace of the warning it never gave or the question it never asked.

On a banking test with 1,000 tasks, checking only the final records made every model look 6.5 to 12 points better than it really was.

And that’s a big blind spot, because an agent can get every record right and still fail the person it’s working for.

So when you test an agent, check what it should have said and asked along the way, as well as what it changed at the end.

biggestContribution.title: Deploy (YC F26) - The Generalist Robot Deployment Company
biggestContribution.text:
Deploy puts generalist robots to work in real businesses as a service. You pay for the work getting done, not the robot.

Generalist robot models can finally handle messy, variable work like returns, kitting, and mixed orders. But a capable model isn’t the same as a robot reliably running a shift on your floor. Deploy closes that gap.

How it works:
→ We break each task into steps and track progress in real time
→ The system knows what’s done, what’s next, and when a robot needs help
→ Every human intervention becomes training data, so robots get better the longer they run

Built by Irene and Sahith, robotics engineers from Honda Research Institute and AeroVect. Backed by Y Combinator (F26).

Run a 3PL, warehouse, or distribution center with work that’s hard to staff or automate? Let’s talk.

biggestContribution.title: Telamont (YC F26) - AI that catches errors in construction drawings
biggestContribution.text:
Errors are hiding between your construction drawings, specs and contracts. Telamont catches them before they reach the field.

If you build, design or own complex construction projects, book a demo.

Telamont (YC F26) catches the errors hiding between construction drawings, specs and contracts the moment they appear, before they become disputes.

Construction projects lose money in the gap between what the documents say and what gets built. The average construction dispute now runs $60.1 million. The #1 cause? Errors and omissions in those same documents, caught too late.

Telamont connects to where construction documents already live and pulls in every file as it lands, continuously building a complete understanding of the project. Every page is checked against the rest of the project, and risks are flagged immediately.

Instead of reviewing documents, teams act on flagged risks, tracking each from detection to resolution while managing exposure and pursuing recovery opportunities across projects.

Charles grew up in a third-generation construction family and saw firsthand how document errors turn into costly disputes. He was previously a software engineer at 1Password. William was previously a software engineer at Poka, where he applied AI to manufacturing operations. Their team includes people from WSP and AtkinsRéalis, two of the world’s largest engineering firms.

Halmos enables biotech teams to get more out of every experiment. 

The world spends roughly $100 billion a year on experimentation in Life-Science. The cost of experiments hinders R&D departments from following new leads, and stops revolutionizing discoveries in less-funded parts of biotechnology like cosmetics, food, and biomaterials.

Halmos reads litterature, fetches models and data from the internet, trains its own models, and simulates the experiments before they are run. In a collaboration, Halmos matched the best performance from a company's wet-lab campaign in an average of 30% fewer evaluations across repeated simulations.

If you run preclinical R&D, process development, assay development, or fermentation/bioprocess optimization, we want to hear from you. Scope an experiment with us at halmoslabs.com or email hi@halmoslabs.com (enterprise inquiries welcome).

biggestContribution.title: horizontal. (YC F26): AI agents that run factory operations
biggestContribution.text:
Every factory will be run by AI agents. We’re building them.

Today the work that keeps production moving is scattered across people, teams and disconnected software. When plans change, materials run short or quality issues appear, factory teams piece together the context and coordinate the response by hand.

horizontal.’s agents take on that operational work inside the systems factories already run, like MES, ERP, quality and maintenance. They replan production around a disruption, investigate quality issues and coordinate order releases across teams and tools. Manufacturers start with one process and add agents over time, building toward a factory that is coordinated end to end.

We’re Jakob Hermeler and Niklas Marxer, two mechanical engineers from ETH Zurich, TUM and Stanford, backed by Y Combinator.

evidence.title: San Francisco’daki arkadaşlarım için gelistirdigim bu yöntem sayesinde arkadaşlarım 20 iş başvurusundan 10 dönüş aldılar.
evidence.text:
San Francisco’daki arkadaşlarım için gelistirdigim bu yöntem sayesinde arkadaşlarım 20 iş başvurusundan 10 dönüş aldılar.
Normalde bu oran 20’de 1’di.

Peki nedir bu yöntem?
1. Çalışma izniniz olduğu veya çalışma izni çıkarılması zor olmayan bir ülkede, iş gerekliliklerinin en azından %50’sini karşıladığınız iş fırsatları bulun.
2. CEO'nun röportajlarını, şirket hakkında çıkan haberleri okuyun. Bu soruları cevaplayın:
Şirketin kısa/ uzun vade hedefleri nelerdir?
Bu hedefler doğrultusunda başvurduğunuz ekip şu an hangi sorunu çözmeye çalışıyordur?
3. Ekibin bu sorunu çözmesine nasıl bir katkınız olacağını, ilk 3 ay içinde neler yapabileceğinizi düşünün.
4. Bir ön yazı hazırlayın:
Ön yazıda neler olmalı?
-- Ekibin hangi sorun üzerine çalıştığını tahmin ettiğinizi söyleyin.
-- İşe başladığınızın ilk üç ayınızda bu sorunu çözmek için neleri yapacağınızı anlatın
-- En sonunda İKİ cümleyle kendinizi tanıtın.
Ön yazıda neler olmamalı?
-- Kendinizi ‘çalışkan’, ‘yenilikçi’ gibi güzel sıfatlarla tanımlamayın.
-- ‘Bu alanda kendimi geliştirmek istiyorum’ gibi söylemlerden kaçının.

Unutmayın… Herkes kendine güzel sıfatlar yakıştırabilir. Ve bu aşamada önemli olan, senin kariyerin için ne istediğin değil, onlara ne sunabileceğin.

5. Bu ön yazıyı ekleyip iş başvurusunu yapın.
6. LinkedIn’den, o ekibin ve ilişkili IK’nın yöneticilerinin isimlerini bulun. Ardından VoilaNorbert gibi sitelerden onların emaillerini bulun. Ön yazınızın mail halini onlara yollayın. (Maile ekleme olarak değil, direk kopyala yapıştır yapın.) (2 kişiye) CV’nizi ise direk maile ekleyin.
7. Hubspot’un email izleme aracını bilgisayarınıza yükleyin. Emailinizin açılıp açılmadığını takip edin. Eğer emailiniz açılmıyorsa o ekipten başka birine veya başka bir IK yöneticisine mailinizi yönlendirin.
8. Eğer mailiniz açılıyorsa ama cevap almıyorsanız, hatırlatma mailleri yollayın. Satışta ‘büyülü’ rakam 5’tir. Evet, utanmaca yok, tatlı hatırlatmalara devam edin. Amacımız bir cevap almak. Ya ‘Hayır’ ya ‘Evet.’

İlginizin ve emeğinizin karşılıksız kalmayacağını, geri dönüşlerinizin arttığını göreceksiniz.

Herkese iyi haftalar diliyorum!

-
'Hayalindeki O İş' adlı 8 sayfalık, ücretsiz e-rehberime ulaşmak isterseniz yorumlardaki linke tıklayabilirsiniz. Kendi işe alım ve iş başvurusu tecrübelerimden ve profesyonel kontaklarımın tecrübelerinden yararlanıp sizler için hazırladım. 👇🏻

Bu hedefler doğrultusunda başvurduğunuz ekip şu an hangi sorunu çözmeye çalışıyordur?
3. Ekibin bu sorunu çözmesine nasıl bir katkınız olacağını, ilk 3 ay içinde neler yapabileceğinizi düşünün.
4. Bir ön yazı hazırlayın:
Ön yazıda neler olmalı?
-- Ekibin hangi sorun üzerine çalıştığını tahmin ettiğinizi söyleyin.
-- İşe başladığınızın ilk üç ayınızda bu sorunu çözmek için neleri yapacağınızı anlatın
-- En sonunda İKİ cümleyle kendinizi tanıtın.
Ön yazıda neler olmamalı?
-- Kendinizi ‘çalışkan’, ‘yenilikçi’ gibi güzel sıfatlarla tanımlamayın.
-- ‘Bu alanda kendimi geliştirmek istiyorum’ gibi söylemlerden kaçının.

Unutmayın… Herkes kendine güzel sıfatlar yakıştırabilir. Ve bu aşamada önemli olan, senin kariyerin için ne istediğin değil, onlara ne sunabileceğin.

5. Bu ön yazıyı ekleyip iş başvurusunu yapın.
6. LinkedIn’den, o ekibin ve ilişkili IK’nın yöneticilerinin isimlerini bulun. Ardından VoilaNorbert gibi sitelerden onların emaillerini bulun. Ön yazınızın mail halini onlara yollayın. (Maile ekleme olarak değil, direk kopyala yapıştır yapın.) (2 kişiye) CV’nizi ise direk maile ekleyin.
7. Hubspot’un email izleme aracını bilgisayarınıza yükleyin. Emailinizin açılıp açılmadığını takip edin. Eğer emailiniz açılmıyorsa o ekipten başka birine veya başka bir IK yöneticisine mailinizi yönlendirin.
8. Eğer mailiniz açılıyorsa ama cevap almıyorsanız, hatırlatma mailleri yollayın. Satışta ‘büyülü’ rakam 5’tir. Evet, utanmaca yok, tatlı hatırlatmalara devam edin. Amacımız bir cevap almak. Ya ‘Hayır’ ya ‘Evet.’

İlginizin ve emeğinizin karşılıksız kalmayacağını, geri dönüşlerinizin arttığını göreceksiniz.

Herkese iyi haftalar diliyorum!

evidence.text:
We got into 
@ycombinator
 to fix how AI makes music.
 
Today we're launching Taan v1-preview, the most controllable foundation music model.

Music models today make catchy tracks, but you can't steer them. Ask for "violin at exactly the 11th second" and they usually skip it. So you regenerate over and over and hope one take fits. 

Taan is trained to fix this.
 
Hum a melody, name exact notes, or hand it an image, a MIDI file, a video or a script. Taan composes music that fits your context and follows your instructions.
 
v1-preview has genre support limited to orchestral and cinematic music, with more genres on the way.

evidence.title: 5 years ago I was on a crowded bus in Turkey when I read the email that broke my heart.
evidence.text:
5 years ago I was on a crowded bus in Turkey when I read the email that broke my heart.
I had managed to get in touch with my dream company from Silicon Valley: Cambly.
And was hoping to build their market in Turkey from scratch.

But the email said…
They wouldn’t invest in Turkey due to the political instability caused by the recent coup attempt...

They offered me to join their affiliate program.
I’d get paid if I brought them users.
I was short on cash. 
All I had was my dream to move to Silicon Valley.

I knew the affiliate program wouldn’t be sustainable.
Instead, I needed a steady paycheck ASAP.
But I still wanted to give it a try and do my best.
I wanted to prove that there was potential in Turkey.
Prove that I was THE ONE for the job.
And hopefully… Change their minds.

Deep inside, I knew it was a risky bet.
And I knew I’d be disappointed in the end.
But I was going to try.

For 2 weeks I called everyone I knew and marketed Cambly.
I asked them to try it and followed up later to see if they were willing to buy.

I launched new social media pages for Cambly.
I published articles and posted on blogs and forums.
I even paid for an advertisement on Linkedin. With my limited cash.
Nothing was succesful.

After two weeks of hustling, failing and getting even more broke,
I sent an email to the founders, saying that I could only bring them 5 paid users.
And that night, I kept telling myself in bed, ‘What a waste of time and money…’

I received an email from them a day later.
It started with ‘You brought 5 paid users?’
I was afraid to read how that sentence would end.
It ended like this:
‘That’s a solid 10% growth in our Turkish market, congrats!’

And now…
I’ve been working at Cambly for more than 5 years.
Cambly is one of the biggest brands in Turkey.
And Turkey is one of the biggest markets for Cambly.

What I want to say is…
Sometimes it might feel like you aren’t getting the opportunities you want.
Obstacles keep getting in the way: The economy, visas, coup attempts, COVID.

But maybe…
You shouldn’t wait for an opportunity to come to you.
You should be the one who goes and creates it…
And remember that everyone has to face those obstacles.
An obstacle might be an opportunity to:
- Eliminate the competition.
- Show your unique strength.
- Build resilience.

I hope 2022 will be filled with opportunities for you!
But if not…
You know what to do. 🙂

evidence.title:
Sirsha and I shut down a software business making $250k a year to build a hardware company. Put $20k of our own money into it, moved to the US with less than 3 months of runway, and eventually got into Y Combinator.

Since the start of our YC batch [Sep 15], we have:
- scaled from 400 to 2,000+ pre-orders
- solved a hard engineering problem [near silent whisper capture]
- added a LED matrix panel onto our ring to make controlling agents super intuitive
- locked in two enterprise pilots for our hardware

Here's our YC launch for antimattr (YC F26).

[problem]
For the last year, while building with voice AI, we kept running into something strange. Voice models work perfectly at home, in a quiet room with no noise. But the moment you step outside, they fall apart. The problem was the background noise. As a result, word error rates go as high as 30%, and the transcription ends up being wrong. Voice models are good enough - the bottleneck is the noise around in real-life environments.

[what we are building]
We are building a voice-first hardware interface to interact with your agents: earbuds that isolate your voice from the noise around you and a ring that controls your agents.
- The earphones use proprietary voice isolation to filter out close to 90 dB of background noise and reduce word error rate from 30% [AirPods] to <5%. So, you can take a clear call from a loud pub, dictate with real accuracy, or even transcribe your calls.
- The ring acts as the perfect controller, allowing you to see and trigger your agents and see what they are up to, right at your fingertips.
- Together, this is the hardware interface for voice.

evidence.text:
Today I'm announcing Workers IO to solve the slowest part of engineering, verification!

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but it still takes significant engineering effort to verify what’s being built.

It’s impossible to predict all scenarios that could lead to a failure and that’s why most expensive failures are found in production.

Workers IO runs millions of simulated production scenarios on your entire system, including dependencies. These simulations run inside a deterministic hypervisor which injects faults like network delays, disk errors, clock skew, and process failures to verify how your system handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows us to systematically explore the state space of the system and perfectly reproduce failures.

We are already helping customers do years worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

If you are working on systems that you can never afford to break, DM me and we can help you battle test them!

evidence.text:
Huang Le (黄乐), aka "Alice Huang." The woman at the center of the Nvidia espionage scandal. 

Here is everything 
@ploid_ai
 found on her.

She's a Chinese national from Hunan, age 42. She did an MA in media management at Hong Kong Baptist University. She was a reporter at Hunan TV and CCTV, assistant to the president of HSBC Private Banking, and VP at state-owned CITIC Securities. She moved into private equity in 2015. Her sister 黄瑜 (Huang Yu) is Shanghai Feiye’s legal rep and a Hexi shareholder whose job was “connecting resources.”

She was partner and GM of Shanghai Hexi Investment Management (上海和熹投资管理). Hexi sits in a web of companies that held a stake in a cybersecurity unit of CETC, the state military-electronics group sanctioned by the US. She raised money off her Jensen connection.

In March 2023 she took over 7Road International in Singapore via Huang Le Limited, renamed it Megaspeed, and called herself CEO. Megaspeed became Nvidia's "core business partner" for GPU cloud in APAC.

From June 2024 to Feb 2026, its Malaysian affiliate bought at least $4.8B of Nvidia servers.

In June 2024, she bet a table of Gigabyte and NetThunder execs she could get Jensen Huang to come. She messaged him. He showed up, took a whiskey shot, and the photo went on the internet.

In March 2025 during GTC week photos taken from her WeChat show the two at a table inside Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters and on a California putting green. Her WeChat album that week: “GTC Wonderful time.”

On May 22, 2025, they left his Computex dinner at 三六食府 in the same car. The next day, she posted on WeChat: "收获满满 快乐多多" (rich harvest, lots of joy).

Jensen's own daughter, Madison Huang, was at this dinner, the one where Alice also kissed him. Madison chatted with her and took group photos. Madison's then-boyfriend, now husband, Nico Caprez was there too. He's a 35-year-old Swiss ex–ski racer who has been an Nvidia VP since January 2026, and the two married in Hawaii in September 2026.

In January of 2026 Jensen flew into China for Nvidia’s Lunar New Year staff party at 浦江淮宴. She was at his table, toasting red wine over the Huangpu river. All of it went on her WeChat.

US surveillance picked up repeated contact with an American. Unmasked, it was the CEO of Nvidia. US officials concluded China's Ministry of State Security had recruited her to collect on him and push Nvidia's lobbying against export controls.

She has never been charged with anything.
Her phone is wiped, WeChat and email have been deleted.

This is what one search on 
@ploid_ai
 returns.

evidence.title: Birinin CV’sindeki o havalı ünvanları görüp
evidence.text:
Birinin CV’sindeki o havalı ünvanları görüp
Kendinizinkiyle karşılaştırdığınız oluyor mu?

CV’mde ‘Co-founder’ yazan tüm işlerde
Parasızdım.
Bilgisizdim.
Çırpınıyordum.

CV’mdeki büyük, prestijli şirketlerde çalışırken
Kaybolmuştum.
Yaptığım işi sevmiyordum.
Ne yapacağımı bilmiyordum.

Oysa ki dışarıdan bir göz CV’me bakınca
‘Ne kadar da güzel bir kariyer’ diyebilir.

Hayatımız lineer değil.
Hep yükselemezsin.
İnişler ve çıkışlar vardır.
Türlü türlü zorluklarla karşılaşırsın.

İşte bunları CV’ye bakıp göremezsin.
CV çıkışları yansıtır.
İnişleri değil.

Kendinde hayatın gerçek yüzünü,
LinkedIn’de hayatın makyajlı yüzünü görüyorsun.

Kimsenin hayatını CV’sinde yazan o ‘geçici’ ünvanlar tanımlamıyor.
Kimse hayatını ‘Ürün Yöneticisi’, ‘Proje Yöneticisi’ olarak yaşamıyor.
Kimse ‘CEO’ oldu diye hayatındaki sorunlardan arınmıyor.
Hayatımızı ünvanımız değil, değerlerimiz tanımlıyor.
Tutkularımız, hayallerimiz tanımlıyor.

O yüzden,
Kimsenin CV’siyle kendi hayatını kıyaslama.
Kendi CV’nle bile.

Ve unutma…
Hayatını şekillendirecek olan,
Şu ana kadar yaptıklarından çok
Bundan sonra yapacakların. Yolculuğun.
İnişlerle ve çıkışlarla dolu olan…
Sevinçlerle ve üzüntülerle…
Sana özgü,
Makyajsız.

-> Aşağıdaki kaynakların hepsi yorumlarda <-
*2021 yılının ‘En İyi Girişimcilik Kitabı’ seçilen kitabımın ücretsiz İlk dört bölümü
*Yurt içi veya yurt dışı hayalindeki işi bulmana yardımcı olacak e-rehberim
*İşinden daha çok kazanmanı sağlayacak ücretsiz e-rehberim

evidence.title: a lot of decision models came out in the last two months. almost all of them work the same way. they read text, wait until the whole input has arrived, and then give you an answer
evidence.text:
a lot of decision models came out in the last two months. almost all of them work the same way. they read text, wait until the whole input has arrived, and then give you an answer

that works for a support ticket. it doesn’t work for a robot, a phone call, or a video feed, where the input never really ends and the decision has to happen while it is still coming in

so we spent half of our YC money training a model:) RightNow takes text, PDFs, images, voice, code, robot state and video, all in one model, and you can stream up to 1M tokens of context into it. it updates its decision as each piece arrives. on text it decides in 30 ms and we will make it less with our kernel optimization

we trained it with what we call Reflex Training. the current decision models read everything first and answer once. RightNow is trained to decide on whatever has arrived so far, to hold back until the evidence is there, and then commit. it serves on what we call Reflex Architecture which keeps a probability for every option and updates it as each part of the input comes in

we call this kind of model “System Zero”. system 1 is fast thinking and system 2 is slow reasoning. system zero is the step that comes before both, which is just deciding

we will publish a technical paper on Reflex Training and Reflex Architecture. the model itself will stay closed source and available via RightNow API

this is our first checkpoint and it’s still a little buggy. we launched it early because the fastest way to make it good is to have people use it:)

evidence.title: Another update: We just raised our Seed Round!
evidence.text:
Another update: We just raised our Seed Round!
And it was led by… 
Y Combinator! 

Just a few weeks after announcing our company launch,
I am incredibly happy to announce that... we closed our round!

We met so many investors on the way.
They kept asking the same question

‘Is teaching AI to people really important?’
‘Won’t AI take all the jobs and automate everything?’

If agents end up doing everything

What are we doing by teaching AI to people?…

Honestly?
I don’t know how the future will unfold.
Neither do they.

But I do know that…

Humans should always be in the loop!

We should understand what AI is doing and how it works.
We should know how to make it more effective.
And safer…

And I will do everything in my power to make that happen!

We found investors who believed in that future, too
And they invested in us!

So join our mission to enable humans! 
Not replace them!

As a next step... 
We are launching our product next week!
An AI coach for every employee!
Technical, non technical... everyone!
To help you with any tools your company has. 
And based on the top use cases!

Please comment below if want to know more about it!

Now… 
With the money we raised, 
And with bunch of responsibilities on our backs,
Back to work! Kevin Law!

To enable humans!

evidence.title:
It’s been 1 month in YC,

So here’s 3 of our biggest takeaways:

1. Be misunderstood than understood by everyone.

So often it is so easy for Clean to say what everyone in the industry does: “AI Sales Platform to grow faster than your competitors”.
Although it may attract customers, it won’t attract the right ones.
We are focused on industries where timing matters the most. 

Powering the sales for manufacturing tech, insurance tech, fintech, legal tech & tech infra.

2. Superior distribution/sales is the biggest moat

This era will be defined by the best way to grow fast and reach an audience that cares.
The one that owns the attention & superior strategy, owns the industry.
The most successful companies in this era will be created by creator-founders.

Be on the lookout for big risk takers (like Clean).

3. Do the hardest things first

At a startup, there’s always countless of things you can do.
There always will be, as a founder it is your duty to focus on the hardest things.
Things that will change the trajectory of the company significantly first.

Because you need to know if that direction will make you fail early rather than later.

YC has already become an insane jump in the progress of Clean (YC F26).

The biggest launch of YC is coming soon…

📸: Us at the OG YC sign in Mountain View.

Excited to share that OpenHack is now part of Y Combinator Fall 2026! 🚀

Feels pretty surreal to be writing this, after building, shipping, selling and figuring things out the hard way.

Despite all advancements in security tooling, organizations still struggle with false positives, knowing what to fix first, and AI-assisted attacks moving faster than ever.

That’s why we’re building an always-on AI security engineer. One that is the most context aware - knowing your business, developer intent and system architecture deeply. It can hunt, reason, prioritize and verify vulnerabilities based on true business impact like a real security engineer.

It’s a much harder problem to solve than it looks on the surface, and we’re just getting started.

Back to building. 🫡

evidence.text:
Introducing Workers IO

Agents are making it possible to turn ideas into software faster than ever. To keep up with that, we need better ways to understand how our software will behave in real-world.

Workers IO runs your entire system through millions of simulated futures, exploring what happens when machines fail, networks slow down, and events arrive in the wrong order. It searches for the combinations that break your system before your customers encounter them.

Every failure it encounters is perfectly reproducible, helping teams understand what happened, work on a fix, and verify against the same scenario.

This ability changes what teams are willing to take on. Difficult engineering decisions become things that you can explore and verify.

That’s the future we’re working toward: small teams building increasingly ambitious systems, with the evidence to stand behind.

I can’t wait to see what you build with that confidence.

evidence.title:
Getting your inference right shouldn't be hard.

Today Lakshmi and I are launching RouterPlus (YC F26), a managed inference marketplace.

Most AI teams we meet already know they are overpaying for inference or hitting limits. What stops them from fixing it is the work: picking the right model, finding a provider that can handle their traffic, and negotiating the capacity. 

RouterPlus does that work for them. We test models on their own traffic, find the provider that runs it best at their scale, and negotiate the capacity and pricing. We manage the setup end to end, including custom deployments, and give you one endpoint to plug into your app.

One of our customers, a consumer app handling around 3 million messages a day, wanted to move from a closed model to an open one. They had already tried several providers. Some served compressed models that hurt quality, and others couldn't hold their traffic. We evaluated models on their own traffic, picked a provider and set up a dedicated deployment. P95 latency went from 4.8 seconds to under 4, at lower cost and the same quality.

We also sourced capacity for a fast growing AI assistant startup at 15x its average traffic after two outages in one week, and pooled demand from several teams into a single deal so each got better terms.

Today we work with AI labs and fast-growing AI companies, and more providers join the marketplace every week.

If inference cost, latency or capacity is holding your team back, comment or check the cal link to book time with us directly. Tell me what you're running, and we'll help you find a better setup.

evidence.title: Kimseye ‘Neler hissettiğini çok iyi biliyorum’ deme lütfen.
evidence.text:
Kimseye ‘Neler hissettiğini çok iyi biliyorum’ deme lütfen.
Çünkü karşındakinin neler hissettiğini bilemezsin.

Geçenlerde ‘narsistik iletişim’ kurduğumu farkettim. 

Bir arkadaşım işini kaybettiğinde yaşadığım başka bir travmayı anlatıyor;
Bir arkadaşım ailesinde sağlık sorunuyla karşılaştığında, hemen kendiminkinden örnekler veriyordum.

Amacım, karşımdakine ‘yalnız’ olmadığını hissettirmekti.
Ama amacıma ulaşamadığımı farkettim.

İletişimde iki tür varmış:
1) Destekleyici
2) Kaydırıcı

1) Eğer karşındakinin söylediklerine verdiğin cevap, karşı tarafı daha çok detay vermeye itiyorsa ‘destekliyici'sin.

2) Eğer verdiğin cevap, iletişimi sana kaydırıyor, kendi deneyimine odaklanıyorsa ‘kaydırıcı’sın.

Sosyolojist Charles Derber bunu ‘narsistik iletişim’ olarak tanımlıyor.
Ve ne yazık ki çoğumuzda var bu. 
Farketmeden de olsa, konuşma sırası bize gelince
Dikkati, ilgiyi kendi üzerimize çekiyoruz.

Mesela bir arkadaşın sana
‘Çok yoğun günlerden geçiyorum’ diye yakınıyorsa
‘Ben de aynen! Şöyle bir şey oldu bugün…’ DEME lütfen. 
İletişimi kendine kaydırma.

Onun yerine:
‘Neden çok yoğunsun? Neler yapman gerekiyor?’ DE.
Karşındakini destekle.

Dr. Singer’ın bir araştırmasına göre karşımızdakinin hislerini anlamamızdaki engellerden biri kendi hislerimizmiş.

Yani karşıdaki işini kaybettiyse ama biz hayatımızda keyifli bir zamandan geçiyorsak, karşımızdakine yeterince empati yapamıyormuşuz.

Ya da karşındaki terfi aldıysa ama biz zor bir zamandan geçiyorsak karşımızdaki için yeterince sevinemiyormuşuz.

Bu durumda…

Karşımızdaki bizimle bir deneyimini paylaşırken ona
‘Ben de aynısını hissettim’
‘Benzerlerini yaşıyorum’

Demeye zaten gerek yok.
Çünkü doğru değil. 
Çok büyük ihtimalle aynılarını hissetmiyorsun. 

Onun yerine izin verelim karşımızdaki konuşsun, hislerini, düşüncelerini anlatsın.

Karşımızdakilere, çevremizdekilere destek olalım.
İletişimi kaydırmayalım,
İletişimi destekleyelim.

-- 
ÜCRETSİZ e-rehberlerime ulaşmak için:
-> "Hayalindeki O İş": Yurt içi veya yurt dışında istediğiniz işi bulmanız için ihtiyacınız olan kaynak. 
-> "10 Adımda Kendi İşinizi Kurmak" Kendi işinizi kurmanıza, alabileceğiniz yatırım kaynaklarına ulaşmanız için gerekli tüm bilgiler.

evidence.title: Geçen cuma günü ofisteydim ve telefonuma bir mesaj geldi.
evidence.text:
Geçen cuma günü ofisteydim ve telefonuma bir mesaj geldi.
‘İstanbul 19. İcra Mahkemesi kararıyla banka hesaplarınız dondurulmuştur.’
Şok oldum.
Araştırınca anladım ki babamın işi için yıllar önce alıp ödeyemediği krediler beni bulmuş.
Aklıma kurumsal hayatımın başındayken istifa etmek, girişimci olmak istediğim zamanlar geldi.
‘Çok stres olursun, garanti bir işin yoksa yapma’ demişti babam.
Onu dinleyip, istifamı ertelemiştim.
Oysa ki çok zaman geçmedi.
Türlü türlü girişimlerde bulundum sonrasında.

Akşamında eve dönüyordum ki aklıma annemle babamın yıllar boyunca yaşadığı anlaşmazlıklar geldi.
Yatağımda onların bağırışlarını dinliyordum her akşam.
Evlilik, ilişki…
Nefret ediyordum hepsinden.
Uzun bir süre.
Oysa ki artık düzenli, sağlıklı bir ilişki içerisindeyim.
Birine güvenmenin, hayatını biriyle birlikte geçirmenin güzelliğine hayranım.

Düşüncelerime devam ettim.
Babamın sağlığını kaybetmesini izlemem geldi aklıma.
Sağlıksız beslenmesi.
Hareket etmemesi.
Ben de çocukken onu örnek aldım.
Bunun normal olduğunu, ailevi bir durum olduğunu düşündüm.
Oysa ki şimdi özel bir koçum var, düzenli spor yapıyor, beslenmeme dikkat ediyorum.

Ve o akşam…
Geçen cuma günü…
Anladım ki
Ailemden çok şey öğrendim.
Dürüstlük.
Çalışkanlık.
Sabır.

Ama ailemden pek çok şeyi de öğrenmedim.
Girişimcilik.
İlişkiler.
Sağlık.

Anladım ki
Ailemiz bizim başlangıç noktamız.
Ama varış noktamız değil.

Anladım ki
Sağ olsunlar, bize onlar verdiler kalemi, kağıdı.
Ama yazdığımız öykü bizim öykümüz.
Baş kahramanı biziz.
Onlar değil...

-- 

Ben de kendi öykümü ilk kitabım 5 Parasız Silikon Vadisi'nde yazdım, ilk iki bölümüne ÜCRETSİZ ulaşmak için linki yorumlarda bulabilirsiniz.

#girişimcilik #sağlık

evidence.title: Yıl 2015, bir iş görüşmesindeyim,
evidence.text:
Yıl 2015, bir iş görüşmesindeyim,
‘Neden ilgileniyorsun bu pozisyonla?’ diye sordular.
‘Doğrusu… Ben başvurmadım, siz ulaştınız’ dedim alayla karışık bir gülümsemeyle.

İşte böyleydim kariyerimin başında.
Kendimle, yaptıklarımla övünüyordum.
Okuduğum okul, çalıştığım şirketler.
Sanki bir insan değil de bir CV’ydim.
Markaydım.

Bundan sonra atacağım adımımın ‘planlı’ olması gerekiyordu.
Konfor alanımdan çıkmaya istekli değildim.
Her şeyi baştan öğrenemezdim, büyük riskler alamazdım.

Yaklaşık üç yıl sonra ilk şokumu yaşadım.
Yöneticimle tartışmaya, istediğim maaşları alamamaya başladım
İçinde bulunduğum endüstriyi sorguladım.
Ve büyük bir yıkım başladı benim için.
Kendimi o işle, o kariyerle bütünleştirmiştim.
Şimdi ne yapacaktım?

evidence.title: Hayatta güzel olan her şeyin, çok çalışmayla geldiğini düşünüyordum.
evidence.text:
Hayatta güzel olan her şeyin, çok çalışmayla geldiğini düşünüyordum.
Ama öyle değilmiş…

Kariyerim boyunca çok uykusuz kaldım.
Akşam 11’de eve gelip, ertesi gün 7’de kalktığım sabahlara alışkındım.
Proje üzerine proje alıyor,
Deadline üzerine deadline biriktiriyordum.

Ama yavaştan farkettim ki
Günde 12 saat çalıştığım günlerde yeterince ‘yaratıcı’ olamıyordum.
İnsan ilişkilerinde içten olamıyor, kendimi doğru ifade edemiyordum.
Evet, operasyonel tüm işleri tamamlıyordum.
Ama büyük resmi görmekte güçlük çekiyordum.
Yeni şeyler yaratamıyordum.

Farkettim ki 
Ben ZOR bir iş yapıyordum, evet.
Ama DEĞERLİ bir iş yapmıyordum.

Günde 12 saat operasyonel bir iş yapmak zordu.
Ama değerli değildi.

Hayatta zor olan çok fazla şey var, özellikle kariyerimizde.
Ama biz çok çaba sarfediyoruz, saatlerce çalışıyoruz, hafta sonları bunu konuşuyoruz diye
Bu zor olan şeyler değerli olmuyor.

DEĞER, zorlukla ölçülmüyor.
DEĞER, yaptığın işin sana ne kadar uyumlu olduğuyla, hayat görüşüne ne kadar paralel olduğuyla, o işe verdiğin saygıyla ölçülüyor.

Bundan sonrası için kendime ve sizlere tavsiyem şu olurdu:

Eğer ki bir dağa tırmanacaksak, o dağın tırmanmaya değer olduğuna emin olalım…

—
Hayalindeki işi bulmak ister misin?
Ya da kendi işini kurmak?

Bu konularda hazırladığım ÜCRETSİZ e-rehberlere yorumlardan ulaşabilirsiniz.

evidence.title: We are building a voice-first hardware interface to interact with your agents: earbuds that isolate your voice from the noise around you and a ring that controls your agents. We have already sold our first batch of hardware and have 2,000+ pre-orders.
evidence.text:
We are building a voice-first hardware interface to interact with your agents: earbuds that isolate your voice from the noise around you and a ring that controls your agents. We have already sold our first batch of hardware and have 2,000+ pre-orders.

[problem]
For the last year, while building with voice AI, we kept running into something strange. Voice models work perfectly at home, in a quiet room with no noise. But the moment you step outside, they fall apart. The problem was the background noise. As a result, word error rates go as high as 30%, and the transcription ends up being wrong. Voice models are good enough - the bottleneck is the noise around in real-life environments.

[what we are building]
We are building a voice-first hardware interface to interact with your agents: earbuds that isolate your voice from the noise around you and a ring that controls your agents.
- The earphones use proprietary voice isolation to filter out close to 90 dB of background noise and reduce word error rate from 30% [AirPods] to <5%. So, you can take a clear call from a loud pub, dictate with real accuracy, or even transcribe your calls.
- The ring acts as the perfect controller, allowing you to see and trigger your agents and see what they are up to, right at your fingertips.
- Together, this is the hardware interface for voice.
